sections.title: Objects and components
sections.text:
# Objects and components

Live lowercase Transform properties expose world and local TRS. Runtime object creation, hierarchy cloning (including compiled script fields and lifecycle), component addition/removal, hierarchy activation, tags and layers are available. Legacy Entity.Transform remains an immutable snapshot. Runtime changes are discarded on Stop. Objects may have one built-in component of each storage kind and one instance of each compiled script path; unsupported component types fail explicitly.

Transforms reject parenting cycles. Native TRS hierarchy cannot represent shear from rotated nonuniform parent scale; use uniform parent scales. Authored asset-backed AudioSource/Animator instances can be cloned and removed; adding either from an empty object still requires an authored asset/configuration. No asset, script source or authored project is created by runtime AddComponent.

Execution and time
sections.text:
# Execution and time

At Play start all initially active scripts receive Awake, then OnEnable, then Start. Scripts added/cloned at runtime receive Awake and OnEnable immediately, and Start before their first update. Disabled behaviours skip Update/FixedUpdate/LateUpdate; deactivating their GameObject also stops coroutines. OnDisable precedes OnDestroy. All Update callbacks finish before LateUpdate begins.

Each real fixed step invokes FixedUpdate, advances the native solver once at 1/60 second, dispatches contacts and resumes WaitForFixedUpdate. Variable Update and coroutines then run, followed by global LateUpdate/end-of-frame waits. Physics has an eight-step catch-up cap. Axiom callbacks are explicit public virtual overrides; Unity private message dispatch is not implemented.

Time supports scaled and unscaled frame time and timeScale in [0,8]. At zero scale Update and unscaled waits continue; physics, scaled waits and Invoke pause. Coroutines support nested IEnumerator, yield null, WaitForSeconds, WaitForSecondsRealtime, WaitUntil, WaitWhile, WaitForFixedUpdate, WaitForEndOfFrame and waiting on Coroutine handles. Invoke/InvokeRepeating accept compiled parameterless void methods; cancellation and query are available. There is no string-based StartCoroutine or arbitrary async Unity resource yield instruction.

# Mathematics

Axiom.Gameplay API reference. Unity naming baseline: Unity 6.3 LTS.

Existing PascalCase names remain supported. Lowercase vector fields and constants are available. Vector numbers use double rather than Unity float. Vector4Int is an Axiom extension. Legacy Vector3.Forward points toward -Z; the Unity-compatible lowercase Vector3.forward points +Z. Axiom cameras look along local -Z. Random wraps the deterministic replay generator; qualify Axiom.Gameplay.Random when System.Random is also in scope. Not every Unity math member is implemented.

sections.text:
# Random

Namespace: `Axiom.Gameplay`

## Description

Deterministic random facade backed by the replay generator. value and floating Range produce bounded samples; integer Range excludes the maximum. InitState resets the shared sequence.

## Use cases

Generate reproducible spawn variation.

## Example

The statements below belong inside a `MonoBehaviour` callback. Add the components/resources mentioned in the use case first.

```csharp
Axiom.Gameplay.Random.InitState(42);
var offset = Axiom.Gameplay.Random.Range(-2.0, 2.0);
Debug.Log(offset);
```

## Compatibility and limitations

Existing PascalCase names remain supported. Lowercase vector fields and constants are available. Vector numbers use double rather than Unity float. Vector4Int is an Axiom extension. Legacy Vector3.Forward points toward -Z; the Unity-compatible lowercase Vector3.forward points +Z. Axiom cameras look along local -Z. Random wraps the deterministic replay generator; qualify Axiom.Gameplay.Random when System.Random is also in scope. Not every Unity math member is implemented.


## Implemented declarations

```csharp
public static class Random {
 public static double value=>ReplayRandom.NextDouble();public static void InitState(int seed)=>ReplayRandom.Reset(unchecked((uint)seed));public static double Range(double min,double max)=>min+(max-min)*value;public static int Range(int min,int max)=>max<=min?min:min+(int)(value*(max-min));
}
```

sections.title: Rigidbody
RigidBody
sections.text:
# RigidBody

Namespace: `Axiom.Gameplay`

## Description

Legacy immutable velocity snapshot. Reading it does not provide a writable component; use Entity.SetVelocity or the live Rigidbody/Rigidbody2D facade to mutate the body.

## Use cases

Preserve vertical speed in existing Axiom controllers.

## Example

The statements below belong inside a `MonoBehaviour` callback. Add the components/resources mentioned in the use case first.

```csharp
var velocity = Entity.RigidBody.Velocity;
Entity.SetVelocity(new Vector3(2, velocity.Y, velocity.Z));
```

## Compatibility and limitations

RigidBody is the legacy velocity snapshot; Rigidbody is the live wrapper. AddForce uses the current frame delta for force/acceleration and directly applies impulse/velocity change; mass comes from the runtime body. Collider bounds return the solver-aligned world AABB of configured spheres/boxes, including orientation. Collider half-extents are already world units and are not multiplied by visual Transform scale. Raycasts use the current sphere/oriented-box solver baseline, layer filtering and a finite default 1000-unit distance; triggers are included. Capsules/meshes currently use their configured box collider. Contact callbacks consume the preceding completed physics snapshot (up to 128 contacts), so delivery is one render frame later and omitted contacts cannot emit callbacks. Full Unity Collision.contacts, joints and arbitrary shape casts remain pending.


## Implemented declarations

```csharp
public readonly record struct RigidBody(Vector3 Velocity) {
 internal static RigidBody Read(JsonElement value) => new(Vector3.Read(value.GetProperty("velocity")));
}
```

sections.text:
# ForceMode

Namespace: `Axiom.Gameplay`

## Description

Selects how Rigidbody.AddForce changes velocity: Force divides by mass and integrates over deltaTime; Acceleration omits mass; Impulse divides by mass without a time factor; VelocityChange omits both.

## Use cases

Apply an instantaneous jump or a sustained acceleration.

## Example

The statements below belong inside a `MonoBehaviour` callback. Add the components/resources mentioned in the use case first.

```csharp
var body = GetComponent<Rigidbody>();
if (body != null) body.AddForce(Vector3.up * 5, ForceMode.VelocityChange);
```

## Compatibility and limitations

RigidBody is the legacy velocity snapshot; Rigidbody is the live wrapper. AddForce uses the current frame delta for force/acceleration and directly applies impulse/velocity change; mass comes from the runtime body. Collider bounds return the solver-aligned world AABB of configured spheres/boxes, including orientation. Collider half-extents are already world units and are not multiplied by visual Transform scale. Raycasts use the current sphere/oriented-box solver baseline, layer filtering and a finite default 1000-unit distance; triggers are included. Capsules/meshes currently use their configured box collider. Contact callbacks consume the preceding completed physics snapshot (up to 128 contacts), so delivery is one render frame later and omitted contacts cannot emit callbacks. Full Unity Collision.contacts, joints and arbitrary shape casts remain pending.


## Implemented declarations

```csharp
public enum ForceMode {Force,Acceleration,Impulse,VelocityChange}
```

# Ray

Namespace: `Axiom.Gameplay`

## Description

Origin and direction data for a ray. GetPoint returns a world point at a distance along the normalized direction.

## Use cases

Visualize or reason about a directional probe.

## Example

The statements below belong inside a `MonoBehaviour` callback. Add the components/resources mentioned in the use case first.

```csharp
var ray = new Ray(transform.position, Vector3.forward);
Debug.Log(ray.GetPoint(2));
```

## Compatibility and limitations

RigidBody is the legacy velocity snapshot; Rigidbody is the live wrapper. AddForce uses the current frame delta for force/acceleration and directly applies impulse/velocity change; mass comes from the runtime body. Collider bounds return the solver-aligned world AABB of configured spheres/boxes, including orientation. Collider half-extents are already world units and are not multiplied by visual Transform scale. Raycasts use the current sphere/oriented-box solver baseline, layer filtering and a finite default 1000-unit distance; triggers are included. Capsules/meshes currently use their configured box collider. Contact callbacks consume the preceding completed physics snapshot (up to 128 contacts), so delivery is one render frame later and omitted contacts cannot emit callbacks. Full Unity Collision.contacts, joints and arbitrary shape casts remain pending.


## Implemented declarations

```csharp
public readonly record struct Ray(Vector3 origin,Vector3 direction) {public Vector3 GetPoint(double distance)=>origin+direction.normalized*distance;}
```

Read-only hit collider, distance, point, normal, transform and attached rigidbody. Ray supplies GetPoint. Zero-length direction returns no hit.

# Physics 3D

Oriented boxes and spheres, ray/line and overlap queries, linear/angular bodies and contact manifolds. Runtime setters affect Play only. Rigidbody without Collider integrates but does not collide or appear in queries.

sections.title: Physics 2D
sections.text:
# Physics 2D

XY oriented boxes and circles, ray/line and overlap queries, force/torque, angular velocity in degrees per second, contact manifolds and dynamic/kinematic control. The native solver uses radians internally; the Rigidbody2D facade converts at its boundary.

sections.title: Touch
sections.text:
# Touch

A read-only frame snapshot with fingerId, bottom-left canvas pixel position, accumulated deltaPosition, phase and pressure. Began/Ended/Canceled last one sampled frame; Stationary reports zero delta. Terminal touches are included once, then removed. No more than ten active pointers. Sample from Input.GetTouch after checking touchCount.

## Implemented declarations

sections.text:
# ResourceRequest and AsyncOperation

Resources.LoadAsync<T> resolves already-resident validated resources; it is immediately done. HTTP subclasses remain pending until host completion. completed event callbacks run when the operation completes, and newly subscribed callbacks run immediately for an already completed operation. These are not scene streaming promises.


## Implemented declarations

```csharp
public sealed class ResourceRequest : AsyncOperation {public Object? asset {get;}internal ResourceRequest(Object? value){asset=value;}}

public class AsyncOperation {public virtual bool isDone=>true;public virtual double progress=>1;private event Action<AsyncOperation>? callbacks;public event Action<AsyncOperation> completed {add{if(isDone)value(this);else callbacks+=value;}remove{callbacks-=value;}}internal void Complete(){callbacks?.Invoke(this);callbacks=null;}}
```

sections.text:
# CustomYieldInstruction

Derive a custom wait with public override bool keepWaiting. The scheduler checks it once per Update after at least one frame. Existing nested enumerators, fixed/end-of-frame waits and scaled/unscaled waits remain supported. General Task/async-await synchronization and Unity editor-specific messages remain pending.


## Implemented declarations

```csharp
public abstract class CustomYieldInstruction : IEnumerator {public abstract bool keepWaiting {get;}public object? Current=>null;public bool MoveNext()=>keepWaiting;public void Reset(){}}
```
